text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Canada and Vietnam signed a protocol on Monday pledging $3 million towards next year's Francophone summit in Hanoi of French speaking nations.
-- The governor of the State Bank Cao Si Kiem has denied rumours about a currency devaluation.
-- Vietnam's marine industry netted 1.1 million tonnes of catch in the first nine months of this year, one and a half times as much as the same period in 1995.
-- A one-month session of the National Assembly begins today in Hanoi with plans to discuss the state budget and the country's five-year development plan.
-- Do Phuong, Director General of the Vietnam News Agency has held talks with his counterpart in China's Xinhua News Agency to strengthen cooperation in economic news, technology and training.
-- A new seaport in the southern province of B!#Ria - Vung Tau started operation last week and will handle 8,000 tonnes of cargo a day.
-- Revenue from private-sector sources in Hanoi reached 65.42 percent of its 1996 target in the first nine months of this year, up 50 percent from the same period last year.
-- Hanoi citizens have raised concerns over corruption, smuggling, social evils and the slow pace of the administrative reform in a meeting with National Assembly deputies. - - - -
-- Flooding in the Mekong Delta has killed 56 people, left twelve missing, destroyed 2,589 hectares of paddy and caused damage worth 510 billion VND ($46.4 million) so far. - - - -
